analysis.title: GS DeGrasse - Desk Bank/Fins EPS Preview 7 Oct 2026
key_insights: Financials EPS season starts Tuesday with JPM, C and WFC reporting in the morning. The desk's main focus areas are capital markets normalization after a strong 2Q26, NII, deposit costs, loan growth, expenses, capital, credit, consumer and agentic AI.
Capital markets: the desk asks how much trading normalizes after a strong 2Q26, and whether 3Q26 investment banking was an air pocket or the start of a longer slowdown.
NII outlooks are in focus after the sharp rise in rates and a more hawkish forward curve. Strong asset growth and fixed-rate asset repricing are weighed against rising deposit costs.
Deposit costs: the desk asks how banks manage them given rate hike expectations and elevated deposit competition, and whether a lag in deposit betas could help 4Q26 net interest margins.

Capital: with less excess capital, strong loan growth and higher rates hitting AOCI, the desk sees potential for more buyback pauses at regionals (similar to USB) or a slower pace at the moneycenter banks.
Credit is benign heading into prints, which supports potential reserve releases. The desk is watching whether the rate move creates early stress, with focus on multifamily CRE.

Financials had a rough September: the sector closed lower in 16 of 21 sessions, tied for the worst month since November 1999. Financials also come into earnings after sharply underperforming the S&P 500. Q4 seasonality has historically been favorable for the sector.

Hedge fund exposure to US Financials has rebounded from the start of last EPS season and enters this quarter around 3-year averages. The US bank long/short ratio has fallen sharply across large caps and regionals, with some rotation into regionals heading into EPS.
The US insurance long/short ratio inflected higher quarter on quarter. The US consumer finance long/short ratio is near 2-year lows.

Sentiment by subsector: large banks mixed, trust banks generally positive, regional banks positioning down from early-summer highs with tactical HF buying ahead of 4Q numbers, consumer finance notably negative, payments warm, exchanges in favor, boutique investment banks among the lowest, commercial carriers and reinsurers negative, personal insurance leaning negative, mortgage originators negative.

Single-stock focus: BAC on NII upside and operating leverage, WFC on near-term NIM and FY26 NII vs the $50bn target, JPM on 2027 operating leverage, C on how front-loaded 2H26 investments affect 2027 expenses, KEY on whether a 3.25% NIM is still achievable, HBAN on whether estimates are derisked after the September guidance reset.

Positioning context: BAC saw a significant sentiment change at the mid-quarter conference, PGR is viewed differently on agentic AI, SCHW has vocal bulls and bears, and TRV is debated with long-only investors leaning bullish and hedge funds leaning bearish.

Earnings reaction history: MS has had the best reaction in 5 of the last 16 quarters and traded higher after 9 of its last 10 prints. WFC has traded lower on 9 of the last 13 prints, USB lower after 9 of 12, AXP lower in 12 of 16, and BLK higher after 7 of 8.

sector_views.rationale: Sentiment is mixed on near-term softness versus 2Q and the longer-term pipeline. The sector has often served as a source of funds for money leaving Financials or rotating to nonbanks.
Sentiment is generally positive as investors see EPS estimates still biased higher, though some question whether 2026 is peak.
Positioning is down from early-summer highs, with tactical HF buying since the mid-quarter conference on a view of near-term upside to 4Q numbers. 2027 remains debated.
Sentiment is notably negative among HF and long-only investors, with a view that the macro backdrop and oil tail risk keep multiples contained.
Sentiment is warm as the group is increasingly viewed as insulated from agentic AI or a winner, and spend trends improved into the end of 3Q.
Sentiment is among the lowest. Near-term numbers are falling after a 3Q activity air pocket, and boutiques have limited levers on comp and non-comp costs to support margins.
Specialists remain negative as pricing stays in focus, though some generalists look at the group for defensive exposure.
Consensus is that the group will not work in the current rate backdrop and estimates need to rebase lower.

earnings_insights: JPM, C and WFC report Tuesday morning, opening the Financials EPS season. No EPS or revenue estimates are given in the report.
WFC: the desk focuses on near-term NIM and deposit costs and on where FY26 NII settles relative to the company's $50bn target.
KEY: the desk asks whether a 3.25% NIM is still achievable.

Earnings reaction history (Bloomberg): WFC has traded lower on 9 of the last 13 prints but averaged +5.5% in the 4 that rose. AXP traded lower in 12 of 16 prints, but its 4 up moves were the largest, averaging +7.85%. BLK rallied after 7 of its last 8 prints, averaging +4.3%. COF traded lower three consecutive quarters after 13 straight positive reactions.
crypto_views: The desk asks whether crypto trading activity is inflecting or the recent pickup is a flash in the pan.

Market structure questions include institutional adoption of tokenization and new products such as event contracts and perpetual futures. Exchange sentiment is favorable despite uncertainty over how market structure may change.
risk_factors: Sharp rise in rates and a more hawkish forward curve could pressure loan growth, capital markets activity, sponsor activity, CRE transactions and debt issuance.
Higher oil prices and rates may weigh on consumer health and spend, and are a tail risk for consumer finance.
Higher rates affect AOCI and could prompt more buyback pauses at regionals.
Early credit stress from the rate move, particularly in multifamily CRE.
Agentic AI could affect deposits, funding costs, profitability and customer growth for banks, brokers, wealth managers and insurers.
Soft P&C pricing cycle and potentially high 3Q storm losses for personal insurance.
Sponsor activity and alternative asset manager activity could slow on the macro and rates backdrop.
vol_and_positioning: HF exposure to US Financials is around 3-year averages, rebounded from the start of last EPS season.
US bank long/short ratio has fallen sharply for both large caps and regionals, with some rotation into regionals ahead of EPS.
US insurance long/short ratio inflected higher quarter on quarter. US consumer finance long/short ratio is near 2-year lows.
Alternative asset managers: HF positioning is whipping around as the market digests rates, with specialists trying to buy on weakness but less confident than in August.
Traditional asset managers are favored by HFs and have served as a risk-on hideout during narrative volatility. BLK longs are frustrated that stock performance has not matched fundamentals.
Financials closed lower in 16 of 21 September sessions, tied with November 1999 for the worst month by that measure (price returns only).

tension_points.bull_case: Strong asset growth, fixed-rate asset repricing and a possible deposit beta lag could benefit 4Q26 NIMs and let better NII flow through to the bottom line at asset-sensitive banks.
tension_points.bear_case: Rate hike expectations and elevated deposit competition push deposit costs higher, and slower capital markets may limit expense levers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Banks guiding to higher deposit costs or lower NII on the Tuesday prints (WFC FY26 NII versus the $50bn target, KEY NIM versus 3.25%).

tension_points.bull_case: Hedge funds have been buying since the mid-quarter conference on a view of near-term upside to 4Q numbers.
tension_points.bear_case: The buying looks tactical and 2027 remains debated. Higher rates hit AOCI and could trigger buyback pauses similar to USB.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Regional banks announcing buyback pauses or guidance resets at the 4Q prints.
